messages:
carmen: Heads up — seeing a big latency spike in the eval-runner during the new quant experiments. KV cache saturation + big eviction stalls, DLQ (dead-letter) count climbing. Anyone available to triage?

alice: On it. Do you have the log snippet? Is this hitting canary or prod?

carmen: Canary first, but looks like a cascade into the dedicated runners. Logs:
```
WARN  kvcache: eviction_loop blocked for 23.4s, queue_len=6217
ERROR eval-runner.dispatch: shard=12 dispatch failed -> DeadLetter: no worker available
TRACE rpc.send: to=worker-45 timeout after 15s
INFO  lease_manager: hold_time=120s shard=12
```

ben: eviction_loop blocked + huge queue_len — that suggests eviction is synchronous and stalls the event loop under pressure. We flipped kvcache.watermark to 0.9 in the last canary tune, could be related.

alice: Also seeing long LeaseManager holds which will prevent shards from reassigning. If leases don't time out, requests pile up and get DLQ'd.

dinesh: Quick mitigation we can roll: lower kvcache.max_entries and reduce lease timeout so stuck shards release faster. I can patch the configmap and rollout to canary.

carmen: Doing that now: will set kvcache.max_entries 200000 (was 1_000_000) and lease.timeout 15s (was 120s). Patching k8s config/eng-ml/kvcache-tuning.

deploy-bot: Started rollout of config/eng-ml/kvcache-tuning v2026-03-20-a -> 1/3 pods updated.

alice: After the config change to canary pod, latency dropped back to baseline and DLQ stopped increasing. Canary logs show eviction_loop still runs but queue_len < 2000.

ben: Good. We should still push a code fix — eviction is doing a synchronous flush that can block the runner thread under high pressure. Proposal: make eviction async and add a bounded eviction queue with backpressure signals.

carmen: Agreed. Also want a metric for eviction backlog and a dashboard alert if it exceeds 5k.

ben: I opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/2845 "kvcache: async eviction + eviction_queue metrics" with tests and a feature flag.

dinesh: I'll add an ad-hoc CI job that simulates severe cache pressure (small cache size) to prevent regressions. Will also add a dashboard panel: kvcache.eviction_backlog with alert at 5000.

alice: For the postmortem/lessons: 1) config-only mitigations are fine short-term but we need code-level safeguards; 2) add an integration test that runs quant_onboard_full and quant-ci-batchtime under constrained cache; 3) propagate a metric that increments on DeadLetter so we can alert earlier.

carmen: I'll draft the incident note and include the canary timeline + mitigations. Quick notes: root cause = synchronous eviction + too-high cache size under new workload pattern -> GC/lock contention -> lease hold growth -> DLQ.

ben: +1. After PR merges, let's schedule a small maintenance window to roll the fix to prod.

dinesh: Done on dashboards + CI tasks (tickets created).

carmen: Thanks everyone. Follow-up: I'll post a short summary in #incidents and update the eval harness runbook with a section on kvcache signals. :thumbsup:
